The Criminal Original Petition has been filed to quash the First Information Report in Crime No.212 of 2023 on the file of the first respondent Police.
2. The case of the prosecution is that the first petitioner had sexual relationship with the second respondent/defacto complainant promising to marry her and thereafter, he refused to marry.
On the intervention of police, the first petitioner married the second respondent and thereafter, he demanded more dowry.
The same was questioned by the second respondent's parents, but the petitioners scolded and threatened them.
Hence, the complaint.

3. When the matter is taken up for hearing today, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the second respondent has lodged a complaint before the first respondent Police a n d o n t h a t b a s i s , F . I . R . c a m e t o b e r e g i s t e r e d i n C r i m e N o .

2 1 2 o f 2 0 2 3 ,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.17454 of 2024 dated 05.12.2023 for the offences under Sections 147, 417, 498(A), 120B and 506(i) of IPC and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
against the petitioners.
4. The case is still under the investigation.
By passage of time, the parties have decided to bury their hatchet and compromise the dispute amicably among themselves.
5. A Joint Memo of Compromise, dated 18.10.2024, has been filed before this Court, which has been signed by the petitioners and the second respondent and also by their respective counsel.

The petitioners and the second respondent were also present in person before this Court and they were identified by Mr.K.Muruganantham, SSI of Police, Thiruppalaikudi Police Station, Ramnad District,
as well as by the learned counsels appearing for the parties.
This Court also enquired both the parties and was satisfied that the parties have come to an amicable settlement between themselves.

6. In the instant case, where the parties have compromised the matter, the High Court has power to quash the complaint for the offences https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.17454 of 2024 under Sections 147, 417, 498(A), 120B and 506(i) of IPC and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act .

7. The legal position expressed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in (2012)10 SCC 303 and Parbatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Vs. State of Gujarat) reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641 were taken into consideration.
